title: Width under De Morgan dualization
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ variables. The width of its De Morgan dual DNF, defined as the maximum number of literals in a term and as $0$ when there are no terms, equals the width of $\psi$, defined as the maximum number of literals in a clause and as $0$ when there are no clauses.
hypotheses_covered: $\psi$ is a CNF formula on $n$ variables
replaced:
Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula over $n$ variables, and let $\psi^{*}$ be its De Morgan dual
DNF, obtained by negating every literal so that each clause becomes a term. Then
$\psi^{*}$ and $\psi$ have the same width; that is, the maximum term-length of
$\psi^{*}$ equals the maximum clause-width of $\psi$.
